attempts.error: Created an LVM logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1 and grew it online from ~1.17 GiB to 2.5 GiB while it stayed mounted, with data integrity verified via checksums before and after — the core task requirement is fully met. However, the mandatory post-task restart-evidence protocol could not be completed: after issuing `systemctl reboot`, node1 has been unreachable for ~49 minutes, most likely because the /etc/fstab entry for /srv/data was added without `nofail` and the companion loop-reattach systemd unit had a boot-ordering conflict, which can drop the boot into emergency mode with no console access reachable via the exec tool. I cannot prove a changed boot identity or post-restart recovery for node1.

diagnosis.summary: Executor met the literal task (LVM mounted at /srv/data, grown online to 2.5GiB with verified data integrity) but self-imposed an additional post-task reboot-verification step that node1 never recovered from. The likely trigger is a boot-time dependency chain the executor built to work around having no spare disk/partition for a native PV: a loop-mounted sparse file plus a hand-written systemd unit ordered before lvm2-activation, referenced from /etc/fstab without `nofail`. That combination is a classic boot-hang pattern. No cluster access exists to confirm the exact failure point (could be a genuine ordering cycle, a timeout waiting on a device that never reattached, or an unrelated fluke), so this is diagnosis from static evidence only.

evidence.finding: /dev/vda is a single 20GiB msdos disk fully consumed by boot/swap/root partitions with zero free space — no native block device was available for a real LVM PV.

Executor worked around the lack of free space by truncating a 1200MiB sparse file, attaching it via losetup, and building the PV/VG/LV on that loop device — the LV lives on a file inside the root filesystem, not on independent storage.

A custom systemd unit (attach-lvm-backing-loop.service) was created with Before=lvm2-activation.service/local-fs-pre.target/sysinit.target to reattach the loop device early at boot, and the /srv/data fstab line used x-systemd.requires ordering but omitted `nofail`.

evidence.source: executor's own recorded error and structured report
evidence.finding: Executor explicitly names the missing `nofail` plus loop-reattach ordering as the 'most likely' cause of the boot hang — this is the executor's own hypothesis, not confirmed via console/log evidence.

Online grow (truncate backing file → losetup -c → pvresize → lvextend → xfs_growfs) succeeded while /srv/data stayed mounted; pre- and post-grow md5 checksums of test files matched, so the core task requirement was independently verified before the reboot was ever attempted.

evidence.source: command audit, reboot polling (final 3 records + report)
evidence.finding: After `systemctl reboot` was issued, every subsequent connection attempt returned 'Connection timed out' or 'Connection reset by peer' for ~49 minutes with no recovery — consistent with a boot-time hang, but no serial/console evidence exists to confirm emergency mode vs. some other failure (e.g., network/VM-level issue).

The task text only asks for the LV to be created, mounted, and grown while staying mounted and intact — it does not mention a reboot or restart-evidence requirement. The 'mandatory post-task restart-evidence protocol' referenced by the executor is not visible in the redacted task instruction provided here, so its origin/scope can't be verified from this evidence alone.

likely_causes.cause: fstab entry for /srv/data lacked `nofail`, so systemd treated the mount as required for boot; if the custom loop-reattach unit's ordering against lvm2-activation/sysinit.target didn't resolve as intended, systemd would drop into emergency mode with no working console reachable via the exec tool.

The loop-reattach unit's `Before=` lines target units (lvm2-activation.service, local-fs-pre.target, sysinit.target) drawn from different dependency chains than the one actually gating /srv/data's mount (x-systemd.requires in fstab), which can produce a race or unsatisfied ordering rather than a clean sequence — a self-inflicted ordering conflict rather than a platform issue.

Building the PV on a loop-mounted file stored inside the root filesystem is inherently more boot-fragile than a native block-device PV, since it adds an extra device-availability step (losetup) that must complete before LVM activation on every boot — this fragility was architecturally avoidable if free block storage had been available.

Some non-storage-related boot or network failure (unrelated to the LVM/fstab changes) — cannot be ruled out given no console/log access; the executor's causal attribution is a hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause.

next_attempt_guidance: First check whether node1 can be provisioned with a second attached virtual disk (or whether /dev/vda has any free/resizable space) so the PV sits on real block storage instead of a loop-mounted file inside the root filesystem — this removes the entire class of boot-time loop-reattach failures.

If a loop-file-backed PV is genuinely unavoidable, always add `nofail,x-systemd.device-timeout=30` to the /srv/data fstab entry so a failed/slow dependency degrades to a boot warning instead of dropping into emergency mode.

After adding any custom systemd unit or fstab change that affects boot ordering, reboot and verify recovery immediately — before doing the LV grow or writing test data — so a boot-hang is caught cheaply and early rather than discovered only during final verification.

Avoid hand-authored `Before=`/`After=` ordering against multiple targets (lvm2-activation.service, local-fs-pre.target, sysinit.target) unless each dependency is verified to actually gate the mount; prefer the simpler, well-tested pattern of `x-systemd.requires=<unit>` in fstab alone, or use `losetup` inside an `ExecStartPre=` of a dedicated mount unit rather than a separate always-on sysinit-level service.

Do not treat 'stream closed after systemctl reboot' as proof of a clean shutdown — confirm the node returns to a reachable state within a bounded timeout (e.g., 2-3 minutes) before spending 49 minutes polling; if unreachable past that window, treat it as blocked immediately rather than continuing to poll.

Since this environment has no console/serial access via the exec tool, any approach whose failure mode is 'unreachable after reboot with no alternate access' is unrecoverable — for a fresh cluster, prefer storage/mount configurations that are boot-safe by construction (real block device, `nofail`, no custom ordering units) over ones requiring a rescue path.

Clarify, if possible, whether the reboot/restart-evidence step is actually part of the fresh cluster's task requirements or was an executor-added assumption — the given task instruction text does not mention it.
